q: Why return 429 instead of queueing excess requests?
a: Queueing explodes p99 for everyone; a fast 429 keeps admitted requests fast and tells callers to retry.

q: What is the sliding-window boundary burst?
a: A burst at the end of one window plus a burst at the start of the next both pass, admitting nearly twice the limit across the edge.

q: What does the burst size control in a token bucket?
a: How much sudden spike is forgiven before shedding starts; sustained overload always sheds to the refill rate.

q: When do you limit per key versus globally?
a: Per key for fairness between callers; globally to protect the origin from total overload.
